scope: US personnel deaths relevant to Pacific force-generation and historical-vs-Branch comparison. Ground, shipboard, and aircrew are separated where possible. POW/WIA are not silently converted into deaths.
accounting_rules: Use an umbrella historical campaign total only once; do not also add its named ship/battle components.
A historical death avoided is a credit only after the historical event is actually absent on the active Branch path.
A survivor is not automatically a deployable replacement: POW, WIA, disease, unit reconstitution, training, and theater commitment remain separate.
Carrier hull loss does not imply air group or deck crew annihilation; rescue geometry is event-specific.
For events whose current settlement gives total casualties but no fatality split, carry a bounded WORKING_FATALITY_RECONSTRUCTION rather than inventing an exact KIA number.
Specialist value is tracked separately: line infantry/NCO, surface-ship crew, carrier deck crew, and aircrew are not interchangeable manpower.

south_pacific_guadalcanal_replacement_su.interpretation: This is the correct first-order 'subtract Guadalcanal' credit. It is not the final national manpower delta because Branch Midway and later branch battles add deaths elsewhere.

specialist_manpower_implication.national_US_manpower: A few thousand net deaths do not by themselves alter U.S. national mobilization or division authorization.
specialist_manpower_implication.USMC_and_specific_units: Santo/New Caledonia losses, POWs, and wounded can heavily disrupt specific Marine/Army formations even when national replacements exist.
specialist_manpower_implication.surface_navy: The branch avoids most historical Guadalcanal cruiser/destroyer crew deaths and hull losses. This is operationally more important than the same number of generic Army replacements because experienced ship crews and surviving hulls remain immediately useful.
specialist_manpower_implication.carrier_navy: Branch Midway destroys more fleet-carrier hulls than history and creates a large carrier/deck-crew burden, partially offset by deliberate rescue and by avoiding later Guadalcanal carrier losses.
specialist_manpower_implication.aircrew: Keep separate. Carrier/land aviation deaths and missing require an aircrew lineage ledger; do not infer from aircraft losses one-for-one.

current_use_rule: For force planning after 1944-02-10, do not add a generic +7,100 U.S. manpower bonus. Use unit-specific availability plus this death ledger. The robust qualitative correction is healthier U.S. cruiser/DD manpower and hull availability than historical Guadalcanal, while carrier and South-Pacific ground formations pay alternate branch costs.
